title: Function of the underlined line (fiction/memoir)
subtitle: Text Structure and Purpose · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Text Structure and Purpose are this one** — 6 Easy, 2 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage is introduced with 'The following text is from [author's] [year] novel/memoir/story.' It is only 2-4 sentences long, and one line is underlined.
- The choices describe what that line accomplishes: contrasts two characters, illustrates a feeling, summarizes what came before, or describes an event.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Read the sentence right before and right after the underlined line, since its job is almost always defined by what sits next to it.

- 2) Say in plain words what the line shows, e.g. 'shows the character is different from X' or 'shows a thing means more than its literal use.' 3) Pick the choice that matches that, including any figurative meaning.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Choices take the line too literally, for example reading a symbolic image as a physical fact.
Or they invent content the text never shows, such as a conversation, a dislike, or a list of topics.
Before you pick a choice, check that you can point to the words that support it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
Choices take the line too literally, for example reading a symbolic image as a physical fact.
Or they invent content the text never shows, such as a conversation, a dislike, or a list of topics.
